default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-109.title: Realized-skewness reversal
E-109.hypothesis: A window of 1-bar returns with strong positive skew means the rise came from a few large up bars (chasers and stop bursts) while most bars drifted down; like lottery-like assets, the spiky side is overpaid and liquidity providers lean against it, so the first down bar while skew is high starts the reversal (mirror).

E-110.title: AB=CD measured-move completion fade
E-110.hypothesis: Swing traders project the second leg equal to the first (AB=CD) and park take-profits and harmonic counter-entries at D; when a zigzag leg after a 38-89% pullback reaches D, that resting liquidity absorbs the push and the leg's late buyers are the exit, so fade at D (mirror).

E-111.title: Mass Index reversal bulge
E-111.hypothesis: Dorsey's Mass Index sums the EMA ratio of bar ranges; a bulge above ~27 that falls back means a range expansion has run its course, which tends to end the prevailing swing; trade against the 9-EMA slope at the moment the bulge completes.

E-112.title: Negative Volume Index cross follow
E-112.hypothesis: Fosback's NVI accumulates price change only on bars where volume falls, the bars traded by patient participants rather than the crowd; when that quiet-bar price path breaks clearly away from its own EMA, the patient side is moving price without noise traders, so follow it.

E-113.title: Converging-triangle break follow
E-113.hypothesis: Flat highs with rising lows (ascending triangle) show a fixed seller being met by buyers raising their bids every dip; once that seller is filled and price closes above the flat top, the stops above and the impatient bidders lift it, so follow the break (mirror for a descending triangle).

E-114.title: Calm-dollar WIN extreme fade
E-114.hypothesis: Foreign and macro flow into Brazil moves the dollar and the index together; when WDO has barely moved in the last 30 minutes, a WIN close beyond its recent high/low is local flow without macro backing, which market makers fade back into the range.

E-116.title: Impulsive-vs-corrective body asymmetry follow
E-116.hypothesis: When up bars have much larger bodies than down bars over a window, rises are made by initiative market orders while dips are mere drift (corrective); the impulsive side controls the tape, so follow it when the asymmetry appears with price above its window mean (mirror).

E-117.title: Slow-pullback resumption
E-117.hypothesis: After a fast impulse leg, a pullback that travels much slower than the impulse is passive profit-taking, not new supply; the first bar closing above the previous bar's high shows the impulse side returning before the pullback gains speed, so follow it (mirror).

E-118.title: Close-vs-midpoint divergence fade
E-118.hypothesis: When closes rise over a window but bar midpoints do not, the gains are printed in the last seconds of each bar (closing pushes) while most trading stays where it was; the push is cosmetic and reverts once the pushers stop, so fade it (mirror).

E-115.title: WIN-led dollar catch-up
E-115.hypothesis: Equity risk news reaches the index future first (S&P arbitrage, foreign equity desks); FX dealers re-price the dollar a little later, so a sharp WIN move not yet mirrored by WDO predicts the dollar moving the opposite way; trade WDO against the WIN jump.
